headline: Meridian Power Limited: 20.0% of its own under-implementation pipeline is renewable versus 60.0% of the joint-venture and subsidiary pipeline; 90.0% of the group's renewable pipeline sits in joint ventures and subsidiaries.
why_it_matters: Renewable growth is concentrated in joint ventures and subsidiaries, so parent-only metrics and the parent's own capital plan can mis-describe the group's renewable transition, and exposure to those entities' financing and minority interests matters for valuation.

citation.excerpt: • Meridian Power Limited reported group installed capacity of 12,000 MW on a consolidated basis as on 31 March 2025.
• As on 31 March 2025, Meridian has a commissioned renewable capacity of 900 MW.
• As on 31 March 2025, Meridian's renewable capacity of 2,000 MW is under implementation, including 1,800 MW of renewable projects being developed by joint venture and subsidiary companies.
• As on 31 March 2025, Meridian Power Limited has projects with a total capacity of 4,000 MW under implementation, including 3,000 MW being developed by joint venture and subsidiary companies.
• As on 31 March 2025, Meridian Power Limited has projects with a total capacity of 4,000 MW under implementation, including 3,000 MW being developed by joint venture and subsidiary companies.
• As on 31 March 2025, Meridian's renewable capacity of 2,000 MW is under implementation, including 1,800 MW of renewable projects being developed by joint venture and subsidiary companies.
• Meridian has set a target to achieve 5,000 MW of renewable capacity by 2032.

alternative_explanations: Group (consolidated) reporting already includes these entities, so the split may be organisational rather than economic.
Under-implementation capacity may slip or be re-scoped; the pipeline is not commissioned capacity.
The parent may hold economic interests in the subsidiaries that offset the apparent concentration.
falsification_conditions: The component table in the primary filing does not match the extracted text, so the parent and JV/subsidiary shares differ from those computed here.
A different boundary or date is used for the renewable total than for the pipeline total.
Prior-year disclosures show the same split, implying a structural reporting convention rather than a change.
missing_evidence: Primary-source check of the page 91 table and sentences in the original filing or exchange submission.

Prior-year pipeline composition to test conversion and trend.
Ownership percentage and consolidation treatment of each subsidiary/JV.
